code.originalText: Physical medicine and rehabilitation consultation for a multimodal rehabilitation plan

text.paragraph: Two-week chronic pain follow-up on the day of the rehabilitation consultation. [S]

Ms. Kahlo returns two weeks after her first visit, on the day of her physical medicine and rehabilitation consultation. The rehabilitation plan starts physical therapy twice a week with graded exercise, core and hip strengthening, and aquatic therapy, with a shoe lift for her shorter right leg; her first session is today. She has taken duloxetine 30 mg daily for two weeks. It caused mild nausea for the first few days, which has passed, and no dizziness, sweating, or sleep change. She takes acetaminophen 1 g three times a day and uses the diclofenac gel on her ankle, which makes standing easier. She still takes no more than four oxycodone tablets a day and has needed no early refills. The burning in her right leg is a little less at night. She can stand at the easel for about 15 minutes before the pain makes her sit. She has agreed to a first small reduction in her oxycodone dose at the four-week visit, provided her function holds, and asks that the taper stay slow. [S]
